persona.who: 47, runs the family cash-and-carry in Leicester, second generation, Punjabi background. Father (78) still comes in and overrules him in front of staff.
persona.note: I've run this business for 15 years and my dad still walks in and changes my decisions in front of the staff. I'm 47. He's 78. I can't say anything because it's his business in his head and he's my father

understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call being seen as less than you are, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.week_thesis: From being handed a smaller role in the business you built to holding your ground on what is yours, with the words to say so.

week_beats.hook: You recognise being publicly overridden and the silence you cannot break, named without blame.

understanding.core_struggle: A man of who built a business is being publicly overridden by his -year-old father, and feels he cannot speak up because of the father-son bond.
understanding.mirror: You run a business you built for years, and your father still walks in and changes your decisions in front of your staff.
understanding.insight: You are not asking for too much. You are being handed a smaller picture of yourself than the one you live, and the smallness is theirs.
understanding.mechanism_label: Being seen as less than you are

queries.hook: Being publicly overridden in the business you built, by the man who raised you, and the silence you cannot break because of who he is. I keep fighting with my parents.
queries.diagnose: When others see only a role, their picture is their smallness and not your measure; the harm deepens only when their picture begins to replace your own.
queries.steady: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what he sees; your worth was never his to grant, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.
queries.act: Speak the true thing gently and firmly, hold your ground on what is yours, and do your own duty without shrinking to fit the picture he holds.
queries.story: A son who inherited a name and a business, yet was dismissed by his own father, who stood in his truth and was proven right.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
verse.sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
verse.line: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.
verse.translation: Better is one's own duty, though imperfect, than the duty of another well performed. Doing the work born of one's own nature, one incurs no wrong.
verse.why: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.
verse.misuse: Not 'stick to the role you were born into'. It's about honest fit with your own nature, not caste or family script.

matched.label: My parents' expectations weigh on me

prasang.title: Duties by nature, and their fruit
prasang.summary: After listing duties by varna, Krishna says one reaches perfection through one's own work done as worship, and that one's own path, though imperfect, beats another's, since every undertaking has flaws.
prasang.lesson: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

verse.meaning: Krishna is telling Arjuna that the work born from your own nature is the only work that truly fits you. He says that even if your own path is walked with flaws, it is better than performing someone else's duty perfectly. The work that comes from who you are carries no wrong, no matter how it looks to the world.
verse.for_you: You are carrying a business built by your own hands. Your father is overriding that work in public, and you are swallowing the insult because of the bond between you. This verse says your own nature is your true duty. Your work is not wrong just because someone else is watching it poorly.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Right after naming the five causes of any action, Krishna warns about the person who ignores four of them.
verse.sanskrit: तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः । पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्मतिः ॥
verse.line: If you think you alone made it happen, or alone made it fail, you're not seeing the whole picture.
verse.translation: That being so, whoever, through an untrained understanding, sees himself alone as the doer does not truly see.
verse.why: You are one cause among five; own your part, not the whole outcome.
verse.misuse: Not a way to dodge responsibility; you are still one of the five causes.

prasang.title: What makes an action happen
prasang.summary: Every action has five causes: the setting, the doer, the instruments, the efforts, and providence. Seeing oneself as the only doer is a mistake.
prasang.lesson: You are one cause among five; own your part, not the whole outcome.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna after listing five causes behind every action. He says that the person who believes they alone made something happen or alone caused it to fail does not see the whole picture. The truth is that you are only one cause among five. Your part is real, but it is not the entire story. You are one piece of the puzzle, not the whole design.
verse.for_you: You built this business, but you are not the only cause of its life. See the five causes behind the daily friction. Name your part without claiming the whole outcome. Let the truth of your part hold your ground.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: न त्वेवात्माऽवमन्तव्यः पुरुषेण कदाचन / न ह्यात्मपरिभूतस् भूतिर्भवति शोभना
verse.line: Never look down on yourself. Nothing good grows from self-contempt.
verse.translation: A person should never look down on himself. The one who despises himself never finds real prosperity.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.for_you: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what they see; your worth was never theirs to grant, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर
verse.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
verse.translation: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.for_you: The self cannot be cut, burned or made less; what they see is a role, and you were never only a role.

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on how a free person moves through the world.
verse.sanskrit: प्राप्तकर्मकरो नित्यं शत्रुमित्रसमानदृक् । ईहितानीहितैर्मुक्तो न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ॥ सर्वस्याभिमतं वक्ता चोदितः पेशलोक्तिमान् । आशयज्ञश्च भूतानां संसारे नावसीदति ॥
verse.line: Do the work in front of you, speak gently, read people's hearts, and you won't sink in the world.
verse.translation: Always doing the work that comes, seeing friend and foe alike, free of wanting and not-wanting, such a one neither grieves nor craves. Saying what is agreeable to all, speaking gently when asked, knowing the intent of others' hearts, such a one does not sink in the world.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

prasang.title: How a free person lives
prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

verse.meaning: Ribhu tells Nidagha that a person who is truly free does not get pulled under by the world's currents. They simply take up the work that is in front of them right now. They treat a friend and a foe with the same steady gaze. They let go of wanting things and pushing things away. They speak what is fair and kind, and they read the hearts of others with care. Because they do not cling to outcomes and they move with a calm inside, they do not drown in the world.
verse.for_you: You are carrying the work of your business and the weight of your parents. Let the work in front of you be enough. Speak gently to your father, but let your own care for the business be clear. Do not let his words pull you under.

verse.speaker: Ram
verse.setting: Ram is struck by how Hanuman, a stranger and envoy, has just spoken to them.
verse.sanskrit: अविस्तरमसंदिग्धमविलम्बितमव्यथम्। उरःस्थं कण्ठगं वाक्यं वर्तते मध्यमस्वरम्॥
verse.line: Not too long, not vague, not rushed, not strained, in an even voice: that is how to speak.
verse.translation: His words were not long-winded, not ambiguous, not rushed, not strained; they came from the chest and throat in an even, middle tone.
verse.why: Fear jumps ahead of facts; calm, clear words build trust fast.

prasang.title: Sugriva's fear and Hanuman's first words
prasang.summary: The exiled Sugriva sees two armed strangers and panics, sure his brother has sent assassins. Hanuman calms him and goes in disguise to find out. His speech to the brothers is so clear and gentle that Ram is moved and trusts him at once.
prasang.story_hook: Sugriva saw two archers walking towards his hill and was sure they had come to kill him.
prasang.lesson: Fear jumps ahead of facts; calm, clear words build trust fast.

verse.meaning: Ram watches Hanuman speak to them and sees how the words land. Hanuman did not rush, did not use big words to sound important. He spoke in a steady, middle tone, as if he had all the time in the world. Ram notices that this calm, even speech is what builds trust. When someone speaks clearly and without strain, fear steps back and facts can take their place. That is what Ram notices about Hanuman, and it changes everything.
verse.for_you: When you speak to your father, let your voice come from the middle of your chest. Do not rush to prove your point. Speak the facts of the business in an even tone. Let the truth of what you built stand on its own without you straining to fill the silence.

story.title: Vibhishan speaks up and is kicked
story.story_hook: He told his brother the truth in front of the whole court, and his brother kicked him.
story.summary: Vibhishan, bowing to his brother, advises him to return Sita: good sense and bad sense live in every heart, and Ravana is feeding the wrong one. Ravana kicks him. Vibhishan still says Ravana is like a father to him, and then he leaves, telling him not to blame him.
story.lesson: Say the hard thing with respect; if you are struck for it, you may go.

anchor.speaker: Vibhishan
anchor.setting: Vibhishan, Ravana's younger brother, advises him in open court.
anchor.sanskrit: चौदह भुवन एक पति होई। भूत द्रोह तिष्टइ नहिं सोई॥ गुन सागर नागर नर जोऊ। अलप लोभ भल कहइ न कोऊ ॥
anchor.line: You may be gifted and clever, but even a little greed and people stop calling you good.
anchor.translation: Even a sole master of the fourteen worlds cannot last if he makes enemies of living beings. A person may be an ocean of virtues and clever too, but if he has even a little greed, no one calls him good.
anchor.why: Say the hard thing with respect; if you are struck for it, you may go.

prasang.story_hook: He told his brother the truth in front of the whole court, and his brother kicked him.
prasang.lesson: Say the hard thing with respect; if you are struck for it, you may go.

story.hook_title: Vibhishan told Ravana the truth in front of the court, and Ravana kicked him
story.teaser: Vibhishan told Ravana the truth in front of the court, and Ravana kicked him
story.for_you: Vibhishan spoke the truth to his brother while honoring him, and then he left. You do not have to stay where your worth is refused. You can speak your part with respect, and if the ground is taken from you, you may step away.

script: You are carrying a business you built with your own hands. And your father is overriding that work in public. You are swallowing the insult because of the bond between you. It is a heavy weight to hold.

Arjuna is on a battlefield, his body trembling, his mind torn. He has laid down his bow and told Krishna that he will not fight. He feels that killing his own family is a terrible wrong. And Krishna is telling him that the work born from your own nature is the only work that truly fits you. And Krishna replied:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्, स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम्.
In plain words: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.

Krishna is telling Arjuna that the work born from your own nature is the only work that truly fits you. He says that even if your own path is walked with flaws, it is better than performing someone else's duty perfectly. The work that comes from who you are carries no wrong, no matter how it looks to the world. This is easier said than done, because the bond between you and your father is not just a business tie. It is a lifetime of love and debt.

When your father speaks over you in front of others, feel the insult. It is real. But do not let it become your truth. Your work is born from your own hands. Hold that. Let your own nature be the ground you stand on.
What if your own path, imperfectly walked, is the only one that is truly yours?

depth.life: You built a business with your own hands. Now your father publicly overrides what you did, and you swallow the insult to keep the bond intact. You feel stuck between the man you are and the role you are forced to play.
depth.points: Your nature is your own. You do not need to perform the role your father has written for you to be worthy. The work is yours, and your part in it is not wrong just because he sees it poorly.
depth.practice: Write down one decision you made today in the business that your father did not approve of, and let it stand.
depth.question: What would it mean to let your work speak for itself, even when he looks away?
